It has been represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] since 1987.{{cite web |url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/legislators/?v=province |title=Roster of Philippine legislators |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=May 5, 2020 |archive-date=March 16, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170316064243/http://congress.gov.ph/legislators/?v=province |url-status=dead }} The district is composed of the city of [[Imus]]. It is currently represented in the [[20th Congress of the Philippines|20th Congress]] by [[Adrian Jay Advincula]] of the [[National Unity Party (Philippines)|National Unity Party]] (NUP).{{cite web|url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/members/ |title=House Members |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=May 5, 2020}} The third district previously encompassed the city of [[Tagaytay]] and the adjacent southern Cavite municipalities of [[Alfonso, Cavite|Alfonso]], [[Amadeo, Cavite|Amadeo]], [[General Emilio Aguinaldo, Cavite|General Emilio Aguinaldo]], [[Indang]], [[Magallanes, Cavite|Magallanes]], [[Maragondon]], [[Mendez, Cavite|Mendez]], [[Naic]], [[Silang, Cavite|Silang]], and [[Ternate, Cavite|Ternate]] until the reapportionment took effect in 2010.{{cite PH act|chamber=RA|number=9727|url=https://www.senate.gov.ph/republic_acts/ra%209727.pdf|title=An Act Reapportioning the Province of Cavite into Seven (7) Legislative Districts|publisher=[[Senate of the Philippines]]|date=July 27, 2009|accessdate=May 3, 2020}} == Representation history == {| class="wikitable" ! rowspan="2" | # ! colspan="2" rowspan="2" | Image ! rowspan="2" | Member ! colspan="2" | Term of office ! rowspan="2" | Congress ! rowspan="2" | Party ! rowspan="2" | Electoral history ! rowspan="2" width="33%" | Constituent
